stories.title: Burnham says UK with Ukraine ‘all the way’ despite ‘outrageous threats’ from Russia – Europe live
stories.summary: Burnham continues by saying that “Ukraine has been Europe’s protector, not a drain on our security, but the frontline of keeping Europe safe.” “That’s why I believe the Ukrainian people deserve not just our continued support, but our gratitude and our respect.” He congratulates Ukraine on its Independence Day on behalf of the UK. He repeats that the UK believes recognises Ukraine’s “independence and sovereignty in full,” and believes that “international borders cannot be changed by force.” He tells “the people of this country, from Lviv to Luhansk,… that we are with you in this struggle all the way, heart and soul.” He says he sees “an unbroken country” in Ukraine, as he pledges continued support for Ukraine. “We will continue to build the 100 year partnership between our two countries, bringing together our cities and our schools, our businesses and our communities, learning from each other and growing together for decades to come. And despite Russia’s outrageous threats to my country, we will continue our support for Ukraine’s defence.” As European leaders gathered in Kyiv to mark Ukraine’s Independence Day, less than 100 miles (150 kilometres) north, the city of Chernihiv was attacked by Russian forces. Across three waves of attacks, a Russian drone struck an apartment building, injuring 18, the Chernihiv city council posted on Telegram. Two of the injured were children. UK prime minister Andy Burnham hit back at the Kremlin after Vladimir Putin’s spokesperson Dmitry Peskov accused Britain of adding fuel to the fire of Russia’s war (11:28).

stories.title: South Korea says US cancelled upcoming joint marine exercises over Iran war
stories.summary: Cancellation follows Donald Trump’s surprise order last week to scale back a separate annual joint military exercise. South Korea says the United States has cancelled a large joint amphibious landing exercise scheduled for next month due to constraints on force availability caused by the US-Israel war on Iran. “The US Marine Corps formally notified our forces in June that its ability to deploy forces during this year’s Ssangyong exercise would be constrained due to the situation in the Middle East,” Han Seung-jeon, a spokesman for the South Korean Marine Corps, told reporters at a news briefing on Monday. The biennial Ssangyong drills involve marine forces from South Korea and the US and are designed to strengthen combined operations, typically involving warships, aircraft and ground forces rehearsing amphibious landings. Seoul and Washington were continuing consultations on resuming the amphibious exercise, the spokesman said, without giving details. There was no immediate comment from the Pentagon. The announcement follows US President Donald Trump’s surprise order last week to scale back a separate annual joint military exercise that ended last Friday, citing the cost and Seoul’s refusal to take part in the war on Iran. The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises were cut from 11 days to five. Trump has also sought to revive the relationship he developed with North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un during his first term. He wrote on his Truth Social platform last week that the Ulchi Freedom Shield drills sent “a signal that was totally inappropriate and hostile, to a Country that, as long as Donald J. Trump has been President, has been unthreatening and respectful”. Despite the reduction of the exercises, North Korea fired 10 short-range ballistic missiles last week and issued a statement denouncing the drills.

stories.title: Le Pen could lead rivals in French presidential election — poll
stories.summary: The survey reveals that 38% of respondents are prepared to support Le Pen
article_sentences: PARIS, August 24.

Marine Le Pen, leader of the parliamentary faction of the French National Rally, remains the frontrunner as the 2027 French presidential election approaches, according to a recent poll conducted by Toluna Harris Interactive for the M6 television channel and RTL radio.
The survey reveals that 38% of respondents are prepared to support Le Pen.
Close behind is Jean-Luc Melenchon, founder of the left-wing France Unbowed party, with 16% of voters indicating their intention to back him.

He is notably ahead of centrist candidates and former prime ministers from President Emmanuel Macron’s camp: Edouard Philippe, leader of Horizons, at 14%, and Gabriel Attal, head of Renaissance, at 8%.
The poll was carried out on August 18-19, involving 1,764 participants aged 18 and over.
The first round of the presidential election is scheduled for April 18, 2027.
Should no candidate secure more than 50% of the vote, a runoff will be held on May 2 between the top two contenders.
It is worth noting that Emmanuel Macron, having completed his second term, is ineligible to run again in 2027 due to constitutional restrictions.

stories.title: Former NBA player Enes Kanter ejected after confrontation with WNBA’s Cloud
stories.summary: Kanter was ejected from the Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud on court. Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected after a verbal altercation with WNBA player Natasha Cloud of the Chicago Sky during the third quarter of Chicago’s loss to the visiting Indiana Fever. Kanter Freedom, sitting courtside, stood up and took a few steps towards the court with his arms outstretched after Cloud began pointing and yelling at him at the start of an Indiana timeout on Sunday. A game official and security personnel got between them, and her teammates pulled Cloud away. The official gestured for Kanter Freedom to be ejected, and he was escorted from his seat by team and arena security. Kanter Freedom, 34, wore a black T-shirt that read: “WOMAN noun. Adult human female.” Cloud, 34, spoke with team and league security after the Sky’s 113-90 loss but did not address the media. She did post a statement on social media, per CBS Sports. “To every trans kid/person, You are a part of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved.
